thread:
Alex Kim: quick RFC follow-up re: deployment facade and mode semantics — I want to capture the tradeoffs we discussed and a concrete migration plan. TL;DR: propose a single /v1/infer surface + capability discovery header instead of separate hosted/dedicated/private endpoints.
Maria Singh: can you spell out the compatibility story? customers are already calling mode-specific endpoints today. :thinking:
Alex Kim: yeah — backward compat maintained. plan: 1) add `X-Redwood-Capabilities` response header from control plane describing supported features, 2) keep existing endpoints for 6mo, 3) default routing by tenant metadata. Consumers can opt into capability-driven flows.
Jon Park: how do we signal SLO differences? Dedicated tenants expect latency SLAs and routing guarantees. If we collapse surfaces we need a clear signal so runtime can pick the right execution path.
Alex Kim: good call — include `X-Serving-Profile: hosted|dedicated|private` in control-plane responses and emitted in traces. Runtime uses that for affinity/eviction policies. If omitted, runtime falls back to capability negotiation.
Tara O'Neill: alternative: explicit `Mode` header on the request (clients set it), control plane validates and returns `Serving-Profile`. Pros: explicit intent, simpler routing. Cons: pushes burden to customers and client libraries.
Maria Singh: forcing clients to set `Mode` seems regressive for PLG flows. prefer server-driven negotiation with an escape hatch for edge cases.
Jon Park: what's the incremental rollout look like? we need a togglable translation layer at the edge that maps existing endpoints to the new surface to avoid immediate client changes.
Alex Kim: exactly. implement a translation proxy that:
```
# translation proxy pseudo-config
- inbound /hosted/* -> /v1/infer with header X-Requested-Mode: hosted
- inbound /dedicated/* -> /v1/infer with header X-Requested-Mode: dedicated
- inbound /private/* -> /v1/infer with header X-Requested-Mode: private
```
Alex Kim: the proxy will also emit `X-Serving-Profile` returned from the control plane so we can measure compatibility mismatches.
Tara O'Neill: runtime complexity: we must avoid combinatorial codepaths. prefer a capability bitmask model: runtime checks `supports_streaming`, `supports_kv_cache`, `max_seq_len` rather than branching on mode enum everywhere.
Jon Park: +1. capability-first runtime keeps operational cost predictable. but how do we bill? cost model today is tied to endpoint. we need to carry billing tags through negotiation.
Maria Singh: control plane should return a `billing_tag` in the capability manifest. routing and meterings use that. we already have tag propagation in dedicated flows; reuse it.
Alex Kim: sample capability manifest (control-plane response):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Serving-Profile: dedicated
X-Redwood-Capabilities: streaming=true;kv_cache=true;quantized=false;max_seq=4096
X-Billing-Tag: tenant-commit-2026-Q1
```
Jon Park: telemetry: we need per-tenant SLO counters derived from the manifest. add a manifest version header so runtime metrics can correlate regressions to capability changes.
Alex Kim: add `X-Capability-Manifest-Version` (semver-ish). Also emit manifest id in traces and logs.
Tara O'Neill: ops implications: please document operator config for the translation proxy + how long we keep mode-specific endpoints. recommend 6 months + automatic deprecation warnings in telemetry 30/14/7 days.
Maria Singh: +1. also add a migration SDK helper that can read `X-Redwood-Capabilities` and adapt client behavior (enable/disable streaming, change chunk size). DevEx can ship this.
Jon Park: risk: what if a dedicated tenant's control plane misreports capabilities (bug or stale data)? need a safe fallback to the last-known-good manifest and circuit-breaker to fail to hosted variant.
Alex Kim: yes: runtime policy: prefer control-plane manifest, fallback to local cache, then optionally degrade to hosted-compatible path. We'll track fallback events in tracing and alert on >0.5% fallback rate per tenant.
Tara O'Neill: can we reuse existing feature-gating infra to gate the translation proxy rollout per region/cluster?
Alex Kim: yes. rollout plan: 1) internal dry-run (edge-level only), 2) gate by region with feature flag, 3) open to small customer subset, 4) global.
Maria Singh: who owns docs + SDK? DevEx owns SDK, Product should own migration docs, Runtime + Infra own proxy.
Alex Kim: owners: Alex -> runtime manifest handling, Tara -> proxy infra + rollout, Maria -> migration docs + SDK, Jon -> telemetry + billing propagation. I'll file follow-up RFC PR with the manifest shape and sample proxy configs.
